content:
You own Coeur Mining (CDE) , and on September 23 the stock fell 5.7% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.7%. The worry is whether to sell before it falls further. Here is what is known. Coeur’s last quarterly report showed record revenue, driven in large part by two recently acquired mines, New Afton and Rainy River. The real question is whether those two mines catch up to plan, and what you could lose while they try.

Coeur’s New Mines Are Already Paying Their Way

Coeur’s two new mines already bring in a large share of its cash. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the mines and paying to develop them. In the second quarter of 2026, Coeur’s free cash flow reached a record $388 million. The two new Canadian mines supplied about $175 million of it.

Coeur as a whole is highly profitable. Over the past twelve months, Coeur kept 36% of its revenue as operating profit, against 18.6% for the S&P 500. Operating profit is what is left after mining costs and overheads, before interest and taxes.

Management expects about $1.5 billion of free cash flow for all of 2026. That would equal about 7.5% of Coeur’s $19.9 billion market value. The forecast already assumes lower metal prices in the second half. Coeur is earning that cash while both new mines are still short of full speed.

Why Are Coeur’s New Mines Running Behind Plan?

The new mines are behind plan because ore is coming out more slowly than first assumed. At New Afton, ore output can only rise as fast as the mine’s underground cave grows. Coeur now expects the mine to reach 16,000 tonnes a day early in the fourth quarter. The plan Coeur inherited had it there by the end of the second quarter.

Rainy River has a similar problem underground. Coeur now expects that underground mine to reach 5,000 tonnes a day by year-end, not in the third quarter. The delay matters because its underground ore holds almost three times as much metal per tonne as the open pit.

Coeur’s shares cost 23.4 times the past year’s earnings, close to 22.4 for the S&P 500. That price-to-earnings ratio , or P/E, is the share price divided by a year of profit per share. Those earnings include the first full quarter from New Afton and Rainy River. Both mines were still ramping up then. That quarter’s earnings were also cut by a $140 million non-cash charge from accounting for the purchase of the two mines. If the wider market turns, the stock’s own history shows what a bad stretch can cost .

How Much Could A Bad Stretch Cost You?

Coeur’s worst recent fall came in the 2022 inflation shock, when its shares lost 49%. Each fall here is measured from the stock’s peak to its low within that shock. The S&P 500 fell 24% in the same shock. A $10,000 holding at that peak was worth about $5,100 at the low.

Milder market shocks have hurt too. In the 2023 bond-yield shock, Coeur fell 38% while the S&P 500 fell 9.5%. Coeur has fallen further than the index in all five recent market shocks.

Coeur’s own finances are not the weak point. The company ended June with $1.1 billion in cash, double its level at the end of 2025. Its debt equals just 3.6% of its market value, against 21% for the S&P 500. So the risk to you is the share price, not Coeur’s ability to pay its bills.

The next few months will show which way the new mines go. New Afton is due to reach its 16,000-tonne daily rate early in the fourth quarter. Rainy River’s underground is due to reach 5,000 tonnes a day by year-end.

If both arrive on time, the risk hanging over the new mines shrinks. The $1.5 billion cash forecast would also stay on track. A second delay in the same year would tell you the new mines are harder to run than Coeur planned. Such a delay would also put that cash forecast in doubt.

chineseTitle: 您现在应该出售您的 Coeur 矿业股票吗？
chineseSummary: 您拥有 Coeur Mining (CDE)，9 月 23 日该股下跌 5.7%，而标准普尔 500 指数下跌 0.7%。担心的是是否在进一步下跌之前卖出。这是已知的。 Coeur 的上一季度报告显示了创纪录的收入，这在很大程度上是由最近收购的两个矿山 New Afton 和 Rainy River 推动的。真正的问题是这两个地雷是否能按计划进行，以及当它们尝试时你可能会失去什么。
chineseContent:
您拥有 Coeur Mining (CDE)，9 月 23 日该股下跌 5.7%，而标准普尔 500 指数下跌 0.7%。担心的是是否在进一步下跌之前卖出。这是已知的。 Coeur 的上一季度报告显示了创纪录的收入，这在很大程度上是由最近收购的两个矿山 New Afton 和 Rainy River 推动的。真正的问题是这两个地雷是否能按计划进行，以及当它们尝试时你可能会失去什么。

Coeur 的新矿山已经开始支付费用

Coeur 的两个新矿已经带来了很大一部分现金。自由现金流是指经营矿山并支付开发费用后剩下的现金。 2026年第二季度，Coeur的自由现金流达到创纪录的3.88亿美元。加拿大的两个新矿山供应了约 1.75 亿美元的石油。

Coeur 整体而言利润丰厚。在过去的 12 个月中，Coeur 将其收入的 36% 作为营业利润，而标准普尔 500 指数的这一比例为 18.6%。营业利润是扣除采矿成本和管理费用、扣除利息和税金后剩下的部分。

管理层预计 2026 年全年自由现金流约为 15 亿美元。这相当于 Coeur 199 亿美元市值的约 7.5%。该预测已经假设下半年金属价格将会下跌。 Coeur 正在赚取这笔现金，而这两个新矿仍未能全速运转。

为什么科尔的新矿落后于计划？

新矿山落后于计划，因为矿石开采速度比最初预期的要慢。在新雅富顿，矿石产量的增长速度取决于矿井地下洞穴的增长速度。 Coeur 目前预计第四季度初该矿的日产量将达到 16,000 吨。科尔继承的计划在第二季度末就已经实现了。

雨河地下也有类似的问题。 Coeur 目前预计，到年底，而不是第三季度，地下矿井的日产量将达到 5,000 吨。这种延误很重要，因为其地下矿石每吨的金属含量几乎是露天矿的三倍。

Coeur 的股价是去年收益的 23.4 倍，接近标准普尔 500 指数的 22.4 倍。市盈率（P/E）是股价除以一年每股利润。这些收益包括新雅富顿和雷尼河的第一个完整季度的收益。当时两个矿井仍在开采。该季度的收益还因购买两座矿山的会计处理而减少了 1.4 亿美元的非现金费用。如果大盘出现逆转，该股自身的历史就表明了糟糕的走势会带来多大的代价。

一次糟糕的伸展运动会让您付出多少代价？

Coeur 最近最严重的跌幅发生在 2022 年的通胀冲击中，当时其股价下跌了 49%。这里的每次下跌都是从股票在该冲击中的最高点到最低点来衡量的。标准普尔 500 指数在同一次冲击中下跌了 24%。在高峰时持有 10,000 美元的股票在低点时价值约为 5,100 美元。

较温和的市场冲击也造成了损害。在 2023 年债券收益率冲击中，Coeur 指数下跌 38%，而标准普尔 500 指数下跌 9.5%。在最近五次市场震荡中，Coeur 的跌幅均超过该指数。

科尔自己的财务状况并不是弱点。截至 6 月，该公司拥有 11 亿美元现金，是 2025 年底水平的两倍。其债务仅相当于其市值的 3.6%，而标准普尔 500 指数的这一比例为 21%。因此，您面临的风险是股价，而不是 Coeur 的支付能力。

未来几个月将展示新矿山的走向。新雅富顿预计将在第四季度初达到日产量 16,000 吨。到年底，Rainy River 的地下输送量预计将达到每天 5,000 吨。

如果两者都按时到达，新矿所面临的风险就会缩小。 15 亿美元的现金预测也将保持在正轨上。同年的第二次延误会告诉你，新矿的运营比科尔计划的更难。这样的延迟也会使现金预测受到质疑。
